evidence:
No blocking findings.

Independent final review of PR #1768 at HEAD 44da20a8a5f7ced6e1df4684cf958a842eccf26f, tree 441c026bb0bec8eb3702c46dcec01884c606fdbc, against canonical base 87ec49e8d873863686ee274567305f69db0a65c0. The checkout remained clean and pinned throughout inspection. This is a fresh conclusion for this SHA; the preliminary original-code review supplies historical context only.

I inspected the complete 24-file diff, the actual native/renderer/sidecar execution paths, AGENTS.md, .agents/skills/crystal-ball-feature-workflow/SKILL.md, .codex/agents/independent-reviewer.toml, and the approved design in docs/plans/2026-09-30-r4-sec-001-secret-boundary.md. I was distinct from the implementers and QA owners. Supported launch configuration specifies gpt-6.1-sol with medium reasoning; configuration is not independently signed runtime identity attestation. No further agents were delegated.

The original stale Settings retry finding is repaired. All Settings, boot, reload and recovery producers reach the shared production controller. Each bounded attempt obtains the current optional cache value and a fresh app-lifetime revision while owning the cache mutex, then resolves the confirmed live sidecar target again. No cache mutex spans transport or retry waits. Poisoned cache and revision exhaustion return unavailable rather than an unset; revoked/unconfirmed targets never fall back to the default listener. The existing generation-owned publication and shutdown/liveness guards remain intact.

The production receiver authenticates before reading the body and compares canonical bounded revisions after body reading. Stale/equal revisions return success with zero effects, and per-key highwaters preserve independent key ordering. All existing environment writes, AIS/OpenAQ/ACLED/Cloudflare/S2U credential hooks, module/import/cloud preferences and route/response cache invalidations remain inside the synchronous accepted-update sink. Native missing/malformed revisions and malformed launch floors fail closed. Non-native development retains its unrevisioned contract. Launch snapshots and floors share cache ownership; normal and late confirmation consume the owning generation's delta once, including deletion, through the same current-state sender. Unchanged absent keys retain the existing inherited fallback behavior.

The write-only boundary is coherent: get_secret and its handler/invoke are removed; trusted-window status reads carry presence only, and renderer values are limited to the agreed 17-key allowlist. Renderer loads and writes retain presence without sidecar-only values, and desktop writes no longer relay credentials. Settings/dashboard/wizard/analytics use presence; saved-key verification uses the sidecar's stored candidate with paired credential fallback. I inspected malformed-input handling, credential logging/response paths, retained cache and cancellation hooks, and the relevant renderer consumers. The Tauri configuration adds only the secret-sync helper resource. Cargo manifests, both lockfiles, the publication controller, review-routing configuration and UnifiedSettings remain byte-identical to the canonical base; analytics consent behavior is preserved.

Evidence was audited directly, not accepted from implementation summaries. I read both d154 manifests and every accepted applied diff, expected-red log, restoration record and restored-baseline record. All 44 retained applied attempts (43 accepted plus the rejected first S1 attempt) independently reconstruct their recorded mutated SHA-256 from the frozen production file. Referenced diff/log/restoration hashes match, and restored file hashes match the reviewed files. The accepted set is 22 fresh historical equivalents plus 21 new proofs: 32 behavior, 10 source, one combined source/behavior. Representative genuine observations include N01 10/0 -> 8/2 -> 10/0, N03 and N04 6/0 -> 2/4 -> 6/0, N09 10/0 -> 8/2 -> 10/0, and N21 10/0 -> 9/1 -> 10/0. I checked the named failing assertions, rather than treating an exit code or the deliberate poison-fixture panic as a mutation oracle.

The audited summary final-restorationd154/mutation-proof-summary.json has SHA-256 1d34508d81f1dd985ee32b935e550c6b87e0008623bf557e861042f72f56df52. Its final restored baselines genuinely report 42 Node/TS + 4 native-boundary + 10 controller passes, zero failures (56/0). I independently compared all 5,002 tracked checksum entries with the final checkout: only docs/validation/R4-SEC-001-SECRET-BOUNDARY.md differs from d15434085923a2eccb91248e13946df3cc33a162, and its earlier Git blob matches the freeze checksum. All production/test bytes are therefore bound to the fresh native and mutation evidence.

Recorded validation, not tests run by this reviewer: final-review-freeze-full-gate.json/log pins the reviewed SHA and records exit 0 for the full agentic gate with six targeted scripts. The actual log reports pass/fail groups 21/0, 15/0, 7/0, 19/0, 14/0, 10/0, 56/0 and 643/0 (785 passes total) and ends:
"Agentic validation gate passed."
"Tests run: test:secret-boundary test:sidecar-supervisor test:settings test:analytics-consent test:sidecar-routing test:sidecar"
The log SHA-256 is 427d1532016db2fa231a7a384ab810b6fe91c3eb45d6c56efd01a3fda4419fbb. The separately retained refrozen-native-full.json/log records 97, 9, 44, 7, 24 and 9 passes across six binaries, zero failures (190/0), at the byte-bound d154 freeze; log SHA-256 c2abc6a467d528c6e50a8447f39658b3a20d9ccd7fd2095452d9c9361cfab5c6. all-branch-changed-eslint.json/log records exit 0 on all 17 changed JS/TS files with --max-warnings=0. I checked these raw logs and hashes and the bundle resource audit.

Limits remain explicit. This was offline, read-only inspection; I executed no tests, build, application runtime, native IPC, Keychain/vault access, provider/network call, desktop bundle/install probe or publication, and changed no checkout/index. Source-only proofs establish wiring, not execution of an AppHandle or native IPC. R6 removes one confirmation guard while its secondary live-port guard still fails closed. D1 is a deliberately synthetic suffix mask oracle. The rejected S1 attempt and earlier partial freezes are excluded from the 43 accepted proofs; original September 30 claims remain unattested. The baseline recorder's rustAssertionFailure flag detects the deliberate caught poison-fixture panic even on 10/0 success; actual named failed-test counts and assertions, not that flag alone, support the accepted reds. No real-provider behavior or installed desktop behavior is attested. Best-effort synchronization can still leave temporary unavailability after transport failure, as designed; rollback must keep the native/sidecar protocol pair together. The explicitly accepted renderer-readable credential exposure remains a provider-restriction follow-up.

No confirmed P0-P2 blocker remains in the reviewed diff or its supplied evidence.
